name: Structural fireproofing and passive fire protection
principle: Passive fire protection keeps steel below its critical temperature and confines fire by barriers without any active system: cementitious and epoxy intumescent coatings on structure, fire-rated walls, doors and dampers, deck insulation offshore, and fire-protected cabling or trays. Protection classes follow hydrocarbon fire curves (UL 1709 rather than cellulosic) for process zones; the design allocates fireproofing from fire modelling and layout (API 2218 guidance), and inspection regimes track coating condition because PFP failure is invisible until it is needed.

process_steps.name: Fire protection mapping allocates ratings from layout and fire scenarios
Coating or barrier system selected for the fire curve and duration
Applied on primed, pre-insulated or live-duty steel per system data sheet
Inspection and repair regime tracks adhesion and thickness

limitations: hydrocarbon-rated systems are expensive per square metre; the mapping must be disciplined
coating damage from mechanical impact is common and often repaired poorly
advantages: no activation, no power, no maintenance loop — protection is built in
preserves evacuation time and structural integrity in the first critical minutes
